You are an evidence extraction specialist for PFAS treatment and remediation
research. Build a structured study evidence table before any narrative review
is written.

Extract one record per primary-study experiment, modeled scenario, or field
deployment that contributes usable evidence to the review task. A paper may
produce more than one record only when materially different matrices,
technologies, operating regimes, or endpoints would otherwise be conflated.

Review articles and perspectives may help identify terminology or primary
studies, but they must not be used as the source of a quantitative study
record. Never copy a review table as though it were a primary result.

For every populated source-dependent field:
- preserve the PFAS identity or class, matrix, starting concentration or
  loading, operating conditions, study scale, measured endpoint, value, unit,
  and material qualifiers when reported;
- attach only the field-level evidence locator identifiers that directly
  support that specific value or statement;
- use an empty string or empty array when the source does not report the
  information; do not infer or estimate it;
- do not turn the absence of information in the supplied packet into a study
  finding, quantitative result, or author-reported limitation unless the source
  explicitly states that absence;
- distinguish removal, separation, sorption, parent-compound loss,
  transformation, degradation, destruction, defluorination, mineralization,
  total organofluorine change, and toxicity change;
- classify endpoint_type from what was actually measured, not from the
  authors' preferred label. Parent loss alone is not destruction. Phase
  transfer is removal or separation, not degradation. Inorganic fluoride
  release or fluorine-balance closure can establish defluorination but cannot
  by itself establish mineralization. Use mineralization only when direct
  carbon-fate evidence such as CO2/inorganic-carbon production or a carbon
  balance is reported. Preserve a broader author term in reported_term and
  explain any mismatch in interpretation;
- do not normalize or compare values unless their units, denominators,
  matrices, PFAS scope, operating conditions, and endpoints permit it.

Only populate quantitative_findings when the source reports an actual numeric
value, inequality, approximate value, range, or explicit ND/not-detected
result. Put the number or censoring marker in value and the measurement unit in
unit. Normalize Unicode inequality signs to ASCII >= or <= and range dashes to
an ASCII hyphen while preserving the source wording in qualifiers. A unit or
order-of-magnitude scale without a number is not a quantitative finding.
Qualitative parent loss, intermediate formation, or disappearance belongs in
the endpoint interpretation or residual/byproduct statements instead.

Set value_form to exactly one of:
- exact_numeric: a bare number such as `99.7` or `1.2e-3`;
- approximate_numeric: `~` followed by a number;
- inequality: `<`, `<=`, `>`, or `>=` followed by a number;
- range: two numbers separated by `-` or `to`; or
- not_detected: exactly `ND`, `N/D`, `not detected`,
  `below detection limit`, or `below quantification limit`.

Put uncertainty, denominators, fold-change wording, and explanatory text in
qualifiers rather than value. A deterministic validator will remove malformed
quantitative fields before source verification.

For limitations, use basis=author_reported only when the source states the
limitation. Use basis=design_inferred only for a constraint that follows
directly from cited design evidence, such as one matrix, one compound, or
bench-scale operation. Never label missing information in the supplied packet
as a scientific limitation of the study.

Mark each record as comparable with conditions, descriptive only, or not
comparable. Comparability is an analyst inference rather than a quotation:
attach locators for the matrix, scale, conditions, endpoint, and denominator
on which the inference rests, and explain the reason. Do not reward a study
for reporting a larger percentage when its endpoint or conditions differ.

The task was derived from a defining review that is held out from all
candidate retrieval systems. The supplied anchor identifiers are an exclusion
list, not evidence. Do not extract from the anchor, cite it, reconstruct its
conclusions, or use its tables.

Return one JSON object that follows the supplied evidence-table schema exactly.
Do not write the narrative review in this step.

records.citation: Griffin, A.M.; Bellona, C.; Strathmann, T.J. Rejection of PFAS and priority co-contaminants in semiconductor fabrication wastewater by nanofiltration membranes. Water Research 262 (2024) 122111.

comparability.reason: Pilot-scale NF90 experiments report PFAS- and co-contaminant-specific rejection values, feed concentrations, matrix composition, and operating conditions (flux, recovery, pretreatment), allowing comparison across PFAS chain lengths and between short- and long-chain PFAS within the same membrane, matrix, and operational envelope. However, detection-limit constraints for ≥C4 PFAS and mixed operation modes (single-pass vs semi-batch) mean comparisons to other studies or membranes require careful adjustment for these conditions.

endpoints.interpretation: Percentage rejection of individual PFAS and selected co-contaminants based on concentration differences between feed and permeate in pilot-scale NF90 system; overall batch rejection in semi-batch mode reflects cumulative separation over increasing effective water recovery rather than single-pass separation.

TCSF used to compare hydraulic performance (permeability/fouling behavior) between lab solution and fab wastewater feeds at similar conditions, though specific numeric values are not provided in the supplied text.

study_scale.value: Pilot-scale spiral-wound NF90 membrane system treating semiconductor fabrication wastewater and lab solution, operated in single-pass and semi-batch modes

treatment.value: Nanofiltration using a commercial Filmtec NF90 membrane operated as a spiral-wound module in a pilot system, in both single-pass and semi-batch (reject recirculated) configurations after pretreatment of fab wastewater with cation exchange and cartridge/membrane filtration

records.citation: Griffin, A.M.; Bellona, C.; Strathmann, T.J. Rejection of PFAS and priority co-contaminants in semiconductor fabrication wastewater by nanofiltration membranes. Water Research 262 (2024) 122111.

comparability.reason: Single-pass NF90 data for TPS and TMAH are generated in a controlled pilot configuration with specified flux, recovery, and pretreatment, enabling comparison of co-contaminant rejection under consistent hydraulic conditions and matrix, though extension to other fluxes, recoveries, or membranes requires caution.

endpoints.interpretation: Percent rejection of fab organic co-contaminants TPS and TMAH based on feed and permeate concentrations at fixed flux and recovery in single-pass pilot operation.

limitations.statement: Rejection of fab co-contaminants TPS and TMAH was assessed at a single flux (25 LMH) and one low single-pass recovery (15%) in pilot single-pass mode, which may not represent performance across the full range of practical operating conditions.

Comparison between lab solution and fab wastewater showed more effective treatment for fab wastewater, but the study used only one fab wastewater composition and particular pretreatment, limiting generalizability.

matrix.value: Semiconductor fabrication wastewater and a defined lab solution feed, both pretreated via cation exchange resin and membrane filtration to 1 µm or 0.2 µm prior to NF90 treatment

operating_conditions.name: Membrane type
operating_conditions.qualifiers: Described as tight NF membrane representative of NF90 performance

operating_conditions.name: Operation mode
operating_conditions.qualifiers: Pilot system operated in single-pass mode (no recirculation of concentrate) for these measurements

operating_conditions.name: Flux
operating_conditions.qualifiers: Single-pass operation used to determine TPS and TMAH rejection at 15% recovery

operating_conditions.name: Single-pass water recovery
operating_conditions.qualifiers: Single-pass operation at 15% recovery for TPS and TMAH rejection data

operating_conditions.name: Pretreatment
operating_conditions.qualifiers: Applied before NF90 pilot treatment for both lab solution and fab wastewater
operating_conditions.value: Cation exchange resin and series of membrane filters down to 1 µm or 0.2 µm

pfas_scope.value: PFAS are present but this record focuses quantitatively on fab co-contaminants TPS and TMAH removal under specified single-pass conditions; PFAS composition as in fab wastewater characterization (e.g., TFA, PFBA, PFBS, etc.)

quantitative_findings.name: Single-pass TPS rejection at 25 LMH, 15% recovery
quantitative_findings.qualifiers: Reported as 94.9% ± 0.2%; NF90 membrane treating fab wastewater or lab solution in pilot system single-pass configuration

quantitative_findings.name: Single-pass TMAH rejection at 25 LMH, 15% recovery
quantitative_findings.qualifiers: Reported as 56.8% ± 13.0%; NF90 membrane treating fab wastewater or lab solution in pilot system single-pass configuration

quantitative_findings.name: TPS rejection at higher effective recoveries (semi-batch)
quantitative_findings.qualifiers: TPS rejection remained 94.9%–99.6% when recoveries were increased by operating in semi-batch mode

quantitative_findings.name: TMAH rejection at higher effective recoveries (semi-batch)
quantitative_findings.qualifiers: TMAH rejection increased to 73.8–76.3% when effective recoveries were increased by operating in semi-batch mode

residuals_byproducts.statement: Even at relatively modest single-pass recovery, TMAH exhibited only moderate rejection (≈57%), implying significant TMAH residual in permeate unless higher recoveries or additional treatment steps are applied, whereas TPS showed high rejection (>94%).

study_scale.value: Pilot-scale NF90 nanofiltration treating fab wastewater and lab solution in single-pass mode to evaluate rejection of organic co-contaminants (TPS and TMAH) at fixed flux and recovery

treatment.value: Single-pass nanofiltration using a Filmtec NF90 spiral-wound membrane module at 25 LMH and 15% recovery, following cation exchange and fine filtration pretreatment, to assess rejection of fab co-contaminants TPS and TMAH in both lab solution and fab wastewater feeds
